R5B-deer-walk-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5B-deer-walk-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-5-005 unit 15-118 (official), 500 m SE. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2009 (17 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHws3): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
W facing slope, 22 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 1.8 km NW: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from Stuie, about 70 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.0385, -126.64187, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 1.2 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 523 m, about 75 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2009 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip). Also: black bear (see evidence).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-8, Region 5. Season: mule deer bucks Sept 10 to Nov 30 and more rows (synopsis page 44, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-10, closures 2026-10-16.
R5B-deer-walk-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-8: about 185 hunter days a year for mule deer and white tailed deer (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Beginner friendly
tags.why: Quieter spot only 1.1 km from the parking: fewer hunters, short walk back (Tip, estimate).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).
